title: Coulomb friction: a block pressed on another and slid (implicit mortar contact)
source: Coulomb's law of dry friction: a sliding interface carries μ_k times the normal force against the slip (C. A. Coulomb, Théorie des machines simples, Mém. Math. Phys. Acad. Sci. 10:161–332, 1785; P. Wriggers, Computational Contact Mechanics, 2nd ed., Springer 2006, §5.2)

quantities.quantity: the tangential over the normal force across the sliding interface
quantities.reason: once the interface slips its friction is μ_k N exactly (the return map puts every slipping node's traction on the cone); the force opposes the upper block's motion

quantities.quantity: the tangential contact force on the upper block over the sideways reaction at its top (they balance)
quantities.reason: the friction carries the whole sideways load
a sideways demand far beyond μ N slips the whole interface
